correctness.rationale: A first force in a cubic graph requires a black triple, which has exactly two forms up to symmetry and produces one identical stalled configuration. Any fourth initial vertex able to unlock a second force must belong to the four-neighbour boundary. The eight resulting prototypes equal the five stated orbits and each creates two consecutive full rungs propagating to every vertex. Counting disjoint orbit families gives exactly 13n. Exhaustive 44,322 four-subset tests for n=5..13 agree, but are not used to justify the universal proof.
